q: How many processes and process groups does Process Groups: A Practice Guide describe?
explanation: The practice guide lists 49 processes mapped to five process groups: Initiating, Planning, Executing, Monitoring and Controlling, and Closing.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, Table 1-4

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, Table 1-4

q: Which statement about process groups is correct?
options: Each process group is one phase of the project
Each process group is performed exactly once
They are independent of the project's phases
They apply only to projects with one phase
explanation: Process groups are logical groupings of processes and are independent of project phases. They are not the same as phases, and all five can occur within one phase.

q: Which two processes make up the Initiating process group?
options: Develop Project Charter and Develop Project Management Plan
Develop Project Charter and Identify Stakeholders
Identify Stakeholders and Plan Stakeholder Engagement
explanation: The Initiating process group has two processes: Develop Project Charter and Identify Stakeholders.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 4

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 4

q: What does the Planning process group do?
options: Completes the work defined in the project plan
Obtains authorization to start the project or phase
Tracks, reviews and regulates project performance
Establishes scope and defines the course of action
explanation: The Planning process group contains the processes required to establish the scope of the project, refine the objectives and define the course of action to attain them.

q: In which process group is the work breakdown structure created?
explanation: Create WBS is one of the 24 Planning processes. It belongs to the Scope knowledge area and produces the scope baseline.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 5

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 5

q: A team is selecting sellers and awarding a contract. Which process and process group is this?
options: Plan Procurement Management, in the Planning process group
Control Procurements, in Monitoring and Controlling
Close Project or Phase, in Closing
explanation: Conduct Procurements is the Executing process in which seller responses are obtained, a seller is selected and a contract is awarded.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 6

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 6

q: In which process is a change request approved or rejected?
explanation: Perform Integrated Change Control, in the Monitoring and Controlling process group, is where all change requests are reviewed and approved or rejected.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 7

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 7

q: The customer formally accepts a completed deliverable. Which process is this?
explanation: Validate Scope is the process of formalizing acceptance of the completed deliverables. Control Quality checks that a deliverable is correct before it goes for acceptance.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 7

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 7

q: Which is the only process in the Closing process group?
explanation: The Closing process group contains one process, Close Project or Phase, which finalizes all activities for the project, phase or contract.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 8

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 8

q: Which knowledge area has a process in every one of the five process groups?
explanation: Integration has Develop Project Charter (Initiating), Develop Project Management Plan (Planning), two Executing processes, two Monitoring and Controlling processes and Close Project or Phase (Closing).
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, Table 1-4

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, Table 1-4

q: To which knowledge area do Define Activities and Sequence Activities belong?
explanation: Define Activities, Sequence Activities, Estimate Activity Durations and Develop Schedule are Planning processes of the Schedule knowledge area.

q: How many knowledge areas are there, and which book defines them?
options: 5, in Process Groups: A Practice Guide
10, in the PMBOK Guide, Sixth Edition
12, in the PMBOK Guide, Seventh Edition
7, in the PMBOK Guide, Eighth Edition
explanation: The ten knowledge areas are described in the PMBOK Guide, Sixth Edition. Process Groups: A Practice Guide groups the same 49 processes by process group only.

q: Which of these is a project document, and not a component of the project management plan?
explanation: The risk register is a project document. The risk management plan, the scope baseline and the change management plan are all components of the project management plan.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, Table 1-6

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, Table 1-6

q: In the exam's process reference, which statement describes the project management plan?
options: Why the project is worth the investment
How the project will be executed, monitored, controlled and closed
Who formally authorizes the project to start
Which features the product will have in each release
explanation: The project management plan is the document that describes how the project will be executed, monitored and controlled, and closed. The charter authorizes; the business case justifies.

q: Which four baselines are components of the project management plan?
options: Scope, schedule, cost and performance measurement
Scope, schedule, risk and performance measurement
explanation: The plan includes the scope baseline, schedule baseline, cost baseline and the performance measurement baseline, which integrates the other three.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, Table 1-6

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, Table 1-6

q: "12 of 20 activities are complete and $40,000 has been spent." What is this an example of?
options: A work performance report for the sponsor
explanation: Work performance data are the raw observations and measurements identified while the work is performed. Analyzed in context they become information, and compiled for a purpose they become reports.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, Table 1-4

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, Table 1-4

q: "The project is 10% behind schedule." What is this an example of?
explanation: Work performance information is performance data collected from the controlling processes and analyzed in context, such as the status of deliverables or a variance.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, Table 1-4

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, Table 1-4

q: How do Manage Quality and Control Quality differ?
options: They are two names for one process
Manage Quality is done by the customer
Control Quality is a Planning process
Manage Quality is Executing; Control Quality is Monitoring and Controlling
explanation: Manage Quality is an Executing process concerned with the quality of the process. Control Quality is a Monitoring and Controlling process that checks the deliverables.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, Table 1-4

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, Table 1-4

q: What does "projects drive change" mean?
options: A project moves an organization from its current state to a future state
A project manager approves every change request
A project must change its scope at least once
A project replaces the organization's operations
explanation: From a business perspective, a project is aimed at moving an organization from one state to another to achieve a specific objective: from the current state to the future state.

q: A sponsor withdraws funding halfway through a project. What happens to the project?
options: It continues until the objectives are met
It moves back to the Initiating process group
It ends, because funding is no longer available
It becomes part of ongoing operations
explanation: A project ends when its objectives are achieved or cannot be met, funding is exhausted or no longer available, the need no longer exists, resources are unavailable, or it is terminated.

q: Which process group does Identify Risks belong to?
explanation: Identify Risks is a Planning process. Identify Stakeholders is the one "identify" process that belongs to Initiating.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 5

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 5

q: A team member's skills are being improved through training and team building. Which process is this?
explanation: Develop Team is the Executing process of improving competencies, team member interaction and the overall team environment. Manage Team tracks performance and resolves issues.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 6

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 6

q: Which knowledge areas have no process in the Executing process group?
explanation: Scope, Schedule and Cost have only Planning and Monitoring and Controlling processes. Their work is carried out under Direct and Manage Project Work.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, Table 1-4

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, Table 1-4

q: The exam outline mentions an "integration management plan". Which knowledge area and which process produce the overall plan?
explanation: Integration is the knowledge area that combines and coordinates the others. Its Planning process, Develop Project Management Plan, produces the project management plan that integrates all subsidiary plans and baselines.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 5; PMBOK 6, 1.2.4.6

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 5

q: A hospital keeps its patient records on paper. A project introduces electronic records, and a year later every ward uses them. In the process guide's description of how projects drive change, what is the hospital's condition after the project called?
explanation: A project moves an organization from one state to another to achieve a specific objective. Before the project the organization is in the current state; the desired result of the change is the future state.

q: The only laboratory able to run a project's tests closes for good, and no other can be found. According to the process guide, what follows for the project?
options: It continues, since a project ends only when its objectives are met
It ends, because the resources it needs are no longer available
It becomes an operation, because the work is now ongoing
It moves back to the Initiating process group
explanation: A project ends when its objectives are achieved, will not or cannot be met, funding is exhausted, the need no longer exists, the human or physical resources are no longer available, or it is terminated for legal cause or convenience.

q: A team compares actual progress with the plan, finds a variance and recommends corrective action. A new team member assumes this happens only near the end of the project. In which process group does this work belong, and when is it done?
options: Monitoring and Controlling, throughout the project
Closing, once the deliverables are complete
Executing, during the build phase only
Planning, before any work has started
explanation: The Monitoring and Controlling process group tracks, reviews and regulates progress and performance, and identifies changes needed. Process groups are not phases: this work goes on throughout the project.

q: A project manager brings the scope, schedule, cost, quality, risk and other subsidiary plans together into one document that says how the project will be executed, monitored, controlled and closed. Which process is this, and in which process group?
options: Direct and Manage Project Work, in Executing
Develop Project Management Plan, in Planning
Monitor and Control Project Work, in Monitoring and Controlling
explanation: Develop Project Management Plan is the Planning process of the Integration knowledge area. It defines, prepares and coordinates all plan components into an integrated project management plan.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 5

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 5

q: A project manager emails the monthly report to forty stakeholders, as the communications management plan says. Three weeks later she learns that the finance director never opens it. In the process guide's view of Manage Communications, what has gone wrong?
options: Nothing: the report was sent as the plan requires
The finance director is at fault for not reading what was sent to him on time each month
The process is not met until the information is received by its intended audience
The report should have been sent to fewer people
explanation: Manage Communications goes beyond distributing information. It seeks to ensure that the information has been appropriately generated and formatted and received by the intended audience, and it gives stakeholders the chance to ask for more.

q: The risk register says: "If the import licence is not granted by 1 March, the owner, the procurement lead, switches to the local supplier." On 1 March there is no licence. Which process is now performed, and what does it call for?
options: Implement Risk Responses: the agreed response is carried out as planned
Plan Risk Responses: a new response is designed from the start by the team
Identify Risks: the event is recorded as a new risk
Close Project or Phase: the project cannot continue
explanation: Implement Risk Responses is the process of implementing agreed-upon risk response plans. Its benefit is that the agreed responses are executed as planned.

q: A planned risk response has to be carried out by a department head who does not report to the project manager and is slow to act. Which skill does the process guide name as the tool of Implement Risk Responses?
explanation: The interpersonal and team skill listed for Implement Risk Responses is influencing. Risk owners may be outside the project team, so the project manager often has to influence them to act.

q: Carrying out a planned risk response will add two weeks to the approved schedule. What does the process guide show as the output that handles this?
options: An update to the stakeholder register, sent to every stakeholder for information
A change request, which goes to Perform Integrated Change Control
explanation: Change requests are an output of Implement Risk Responses. A response that affects a baseline is raised as a change request and decided in Perform Integrated Change Control.

q: A key stakeholder who supported the project at the start has grown doubtful and has begun to delay approvals. The project manager meets her, listens, and negotiates a way forward, as the stakeholder engagement plan describes. Which process is this, and what is its benefit?
options: Identify Stakeholders; a complete stakeholder register
Plan Stakeholder Engagement; a written plan for involving stakeholders
Manage Stakeholder Engagement; more support and less resistance
Monitor Communications; an optimal flow of information
explanation: Manage Stakeholder Engagement is communicating and working with stakeholders to meet their needs and expectations, address issues and foster involvement. Its key benefit is that it lets the project manager increase support and minimize resistance.

q: The communications management plan calls for a weekly written report. Halfway through the project the sponsor says he has no time to read it and asks for a ten-minute call instead. What is the appropriate response?
options: Keep sending the report, since the plan cannot change
Adjust the method and update the communications management plan
Stop communicating with the sponsor until he agrees to read the report as planned
Send both the report and a longer monthly report
explanation: Manage Communications should allow for flexibility, adjusting methods and techniques to the changing needs of stakeholders and the project. Updates to the communications management plan are one of its outputs.

q: A project manager must tell the steering committee about a serious overrun. She weighs a short informal note against a formal report, and writing against speaking. Which technique of effective communications management is she applying?
explanation: Choice of media means deciding when to communicate in writing or orally, when to prepare an informal memo or a formal report, and when to use push or pull options and which technology.

q: During a meeting with a hostile supplier, the project manager applies rules of behavior that were agreed earlier in the team charter. Among the tools of Manage Stakeholder Engagement, what are these called?
explanation: Ground rules are a tool of Manage Stakeholder Engagement, with communication skills, meetings, and interpersonal skills such as conflict management, negotiation, and cultural and political awareness.

q: A supplier has delivered everything in its contract eight months before the project ends. The buyer's team confirms the work, settles the final payment and closes the contract. In the process guide, in which process is the contract closed out?
options: Close Project or Phase, in Closing
Control Procurements, in Monitoring and Controlling
explanation: Control Procurements is the process of managing procurement relationships, monitoring contract performance, making changes and corrections as appropriate, and closing out contracts.

q: A project manager is asked what the organization gains from performing Close Project or Phase properly. Which answer gives the key benefits the process guide names?
options: Information is archived, planned work is completed, and team resources are released
Change requests are reviewed, the baselines are updated, and the decisions are communicated
Sellers are selected and the contracts are awarded
Risks are identified and their owners are assigned
explanation: Close Project or Phase finalizes all activities for the project, phase or contract. Its key benefits are that project or phase information is archived, the planned work is completed, and organizational team resources are released for new work.

q: A practice question lists four tools: precedence diagramming method, dependency determination and integration, leads and lags, and the project management information system. Which process of the process guide has exactly these?
explanation: Sequence Activities uses the precedence diagramming method, dependency determination and integration, leads and lags, and the project management information system. Define Activities uses decomposition and rolling wave planning.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 5

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 5

q: A team applies decomposition twice during planning: first to the deliverables, then to the work packages. In which two processes of the process guide is decomposition a tool?
explanation: Decomposition is a tool of Create WBS, where deliverables are divided into work packages, and of Define Activities, where work packages are divided into schedule activities.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 5

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 5

q: A buyer's engineer visits the seller's factory to examine the delivered units against the contract. Inspection is a tool here. In which process of the process guide is this inspection performed?
explanation: Inspection is a tool of three processes: Control Quality (is the deliverable correct), Validate Scope (is it accepted by the customer) and Control Procurements (did the seller deliver what the contract requires). Checking a seller's work against the contract is Control Procurements.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 7

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 7

q: Match each process group with what its processes do.
right: Obtain authorization to start a project or phase
Establish the scope and define the course of action
Complete the work defined in the project management plan
Formally complete the project, phase or contract
explanation: The five process groups are defined by what their processes do, not by when they occur: authorize, plan, do the work, track and regulate it, and formally close.

q: Match each statement with what it is.
left: 12 of 20 activities are finished and $40,000 has been spent
The monthly status dashboard sent to the sponsor
explanation: Data are raw observations and measurements. Information is data analyzed in context, for example compared with the plan. A report compiles information for a purpose, such as prompting a decision.

q: Some tools mark one planning process. Match each tool with its process.
explanation: Decomposition down to work packages belongs to Create WBS, the precedence diagramming method to Sequence Activities, prompt lists to Identify Risks, product analysis to Define Scope, and source selection analysis to Plan Procurement Management.
ref: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 5

links.label: Process Groups: A Practice Guide, section 5

q: The sponsor signs the project charter and the first stakeholders are identified. Select the process group this work belongs to.
explanation: The Initiating process group has two processes: Develop Project Charter and Identify Stakeholders. They define a new project or phase and obtain the authorization to start.

q: The team compares progress with the baselines, and a change request is reviewed and decided. Select the process group this work belongs to.
explanation: Tracking, reviewing and regulating progress, and identifying and starting needed changes, is the work of the Monitoring and Controlling process group. It runs alongside planning and executing.

q: The product has been handed over, and the project is now formally completed. Select the process group this work belongs to.
explanation: The Closing process group formally completes or closes the project, phase or contract. It has one process, Close Project or Phase.

q: The team produces the deliverables set out in the project management plan. Select the process group this work belongs to.
explanation: The Executing process group completes the work defined in the project management plan.

q: What is the project manager's statement?

strip.says: Twelve of the twenty activities are finished, and we have spent $40,000.
Against the plan, that puts us 10% behind schedule.
Shall I put both in the monthly dashboard for the sponsor?

explanation: The analyst's figures are work performance data: raw measurements. Compared with the plan they become work performance information. The dashboard that compiles it for the sponsor is a work performance report.

q: What should the project manager do?

strip.says: The regional director wants our status report every day by phone, not weekly by email.
What does the communications management plan say?
Weekly, by email, to the steering group. It does not mention her.

options: Start the daily calls at once, because a director has asked
Refuse, because an approved plan cannot be changed
Assess the need, then update the plan so that it fits again
Let the team member decide how and when to report to her
explanation: Look in the plan first: who is told, how and when is in the communications management plan. When the plan no longer fits the needs of stakeholders, it is updated. The plan is corrected, not ignored, and not improvised around.
